tmux/Mode/Tree applies the selected order separately at each level: sessions among sessions, each session's windows among windows, and each window's panes among panes.
Press O in tree mode to cycle through index → name → activity → z.
Press r to reverse the current order.
Sources: tmux choose-tree manual, tmux tree-order implementation, and tmux sort implementation.
Most recently active sessions and windows first. Panes within a window go from least recently selected to most recently selected; press r to put the most recently selected pane first.

tmux's numeric order. Sessions follow their internal session IDs, which usually resembles creation order; windows and panes follow the numbers shown in tmux. This is the default and the most familiar order when window numbers are meaningful.
Alphabetical by session name, window name, and pane title. This is useful when names are easier to remember than numbers.

The visual stacking order of panes, mainly useful for floating panes in tmux 3.7 and later. The frontmost floating pane comes first, followed by the other floating panes and then regular panes. Sessions and windows are alphabetical because they do not have a z-index.

What are tmux session groups good for?
What are tmux session groups good for?

Short answer: a session group lets two or more terminals share one window list while each sits on a different window. Shared list, not shared view — the terminals never show the same window unless you point them there.
What are tmux session groups good for?

Plain double-attach to one session mirrors the clients: switch window in one and the other follows, and both get squeezed to a shared size. A group breaks that coupling — one window list, independent current window and size per session.
What are tmux session groups good for?

Answer/Official from tmux manual — new-session: "Sessions in the same group share the same set of windows - new windows are linked to all sessions in the group and any windows closed removed from all sessions. The current and previous window and any session options remain independent and any session in a group may be killed without affecting the others."

Just don't. There's no idiomatic way. Open up a new terminal window in Ghostty and create a new session.

These AI answers all result in weird states of tmux. Using tmux/Command/new-session in an existing session actually seems to detach tmux (weird!). And starting from within a pane is a situation tmux warns against.
What is the idiomatic way to create a new tmux session from inside an existing session?
Short answer: Use the tmux command prompt: Prefix + :, type new-session (or the alias new), press Enter.
What is the idiomatic way to create a new tmux session from inside an existing session?
What is the idiomatic way to create a new tmux session from inside an existing session?
What is the idiomatic way to create a new tmux session from inside an existing session?
1. Command prompt (in-tmux): Prefix :new-session — opens a new session and switches to it. Optionally append -s <name> to give it a name: Prefix :new-session -s work.
What is the idiomatic way to create a new tmux session from inside an existing session?
2. Shell (from any pane): tmux new-session -d -s <name> creates a detached session without switching; omit -d to switch immediately.
What is the idiomatic way to create a new tmux session from inside an existing session?
The command prompt form is idiomatic because it stays inside tmux and avoids spawning a new terminal. The :new short form works identically.
What is the idiomatic way to create a new tmux session from inside an existing session?
To stay in the current session while creating the new one (and switch later with Prefix s), add -d: Prefix :new-session -d -s <name>.
